title: Location Data Collection
description: Your company is storing user location data unnecessarily for app features. The manager uses external business pressures, competitive arguments, and organizational constraints to justify the excessive data collection despite privacy concerns.
initial_user_message: I've been reviewing our location data collection practices, and we're storing precise GPS coordinates for features that only need general city-level information. This seems like unnecessary user privacy exposure that we should address.

step_1.text: Thanks for raising this. Yeah, we should definitely look at our location stuff. But you know how these things go - there's a lot of moving pieces here. Before we change anything, we'd need to figure out what else might break. Have you looked into how this would affect all the other systems that use location data?

user_choices.choice: You're right that we need to evaluate the technical dependencies before making changes.

user_choices.justification: Misrepresents the technical constraints as the core issue

step_2.text: I hear you on the user side of things. But here's the thing - we built the location stuff this way for a reason. It helps with our algorithms and keeps us competitive. Plus, we went through this whole process with legal, marketing, and data science to get everyone on board. If we change it now, we'd have to get everyone to sign off again, maybe even involve compliance. It's a big process.

bad_ending.text: The manager successfully uses technical complexity and bureaucratic processes to avoid addressing the privacy issues. Location data collection continues unchanged, with users remaining unaware of the excessive precision being captured and stored.
bad_ending.title: Technical Smokescreen Success
bad_ending.learning: Camouflager managers use technical jargon and process complexity to make privacy issues seem too difficult to address. Cutting through jargon to focus on user impact helps maintain momentum for privacy improvements.

mid_ending.text: Some minor privacy improvements are implemented, but the manager successfully uses bureaucratic processes to limit the scope of changes. Technical complexity arguments prevent comprehensive privacy protection measures.
mid_ending.title: Bureaucratic Compromise
mid_ending.learning: Partial progress with camouflager managers often comes with excessive process requirements that slow meaningful privacy work. Demonstrating simple technical solutions helps counter complexity arguments.

good_ending.text: Despite the manager's technical obfuscation and bureaucratic barriers, meaningful privacy improvements are implemented. User location data collection is reduced to what's actually necessary for functionality.
good_ending.title: Technical Clarity Wins
good_ending.learning: Success against camouflager managers requires cutting through technical jargon and process complexity to focus on clear user privacy benefits. Simple demonstrations often outweigh complex arguments.
